name: GB300 NVL72 scalable unit (8 racks + 2 network racks)
description: DGX SuperPOD-style scalable unit (SU): 8 gb300-nvl72 racks (576 GPUs, eight separate 72-GPU NVLink domains) in one row with 2 network-rack members in the middle. In 0.6 m slot units, compute racks take one slot each (offsets 0-3 and 8-11) and each 800 mm network rack takes two slots (offsets 4 and 6), so all members are contiguous. NVIDIA's DGX GB300 SuperPOD RA gives ~1.2 MW TDP per SU.
notes: From NVIDIA's DGX SuperPOD RA for DGX GB300: each SU is 8 DGX GB300 NVL72 racks at ~1.2 MW TDP. The compute fabric is a rail-optimized, non-blocking fat tree on Quantum-X800 Q3400-RD (144 x 800G) switches, with 8 leaf switches per SU (4 rails x 2 leaves). Spines are added only beyond one SU (8 spines for 2 SUs, 36 for 8 SUs). The storage/in-band Ethernet fabric adds 4 SN5600 leaves per SU, plus SN2201 out-of-band switches and management/UFM nodes. The network-rack count is an estimate: NVIDIA's rack-layout figure is not in text form. Sizing: 8 racks x 72 ConnectX-8 800G ports = 576 compute-fabric ports. At 1:1, a 144-port leaf has 72 downlinks, so 576 / 72 = 8 leaves, which matches NVIDIA's count and fills one catalog network-rack (8 switches). A second network rack holds the 4 SN5600 Ethernet leaves, OOB and management gear, and room for spines when SUs are combined. Both network racks sit mid-row to shorten leaf cable runs. links is empty because each NVL72 is a self-contained NVLink domain: there is no inter-rack copper scale-up cabling. Scale-out links are derived by the network solver from each rack's scale_out_ports. Some OEM SU layouts differ: Gigabyte's GB300 GIGAPOD uses 16 compute + 8 management racks per SU.
